verdict.rationale: Hyperbrowser doesn't publish a clear acceptable-use/anti-abuse policy in its docs, and when community members pressed on robots.txt/rate-limit compliance, the company added an 'ethical scraping' page reactively — but a hands-on tester found it still doesn't actually support respecting robots.txt or limiting request rate, and Hyperbrowser's own docs promote circumventing bot-detection countermeasures (stealth/CAPTCHA-solving) rather than governing their limits. Missing for 10: an actual published acceptable-use policy document, terms defining permitted use of stealth/CAPTCHA features, and evidence of enforcement matching any stated ethical posture.
